rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near in kin are the relatives of the Prophet; the wayfarer is a weak person lodging with you.
rows.anchor: يعني قرابة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: إِن كُنتُم ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief means affirming God's oneness and believing what He sent down to His servant, the Quran.
rows.anchor: يعني صدقتم بتوحيد الله وصدقتم ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Criterion is Badr, when victory distinguished truth from falsehood and God defeated the polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم النصر فرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers accept God's ruling on booty and its fifth and set their relations right.
rows.anchor: فأقروا الحكم لله في أمر الغنيمة والخمس، وأصلحوا ذات بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers were on the near bank toward Medina; the Meccan polytheists were on the far bank toward Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني من دون الوادي على شاطئ مما يلي المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan was forty riders on the seashore, returning from Syria to Mecca, including Abu Sufyan, Amr ibn al-As, Makhrama ibn Nawfal, and Amr ibn Hisham.
rows.anchor: على ساحل البحر أصحاب العير أربعين راكبا أقبلوا من الشام إلى مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had believers and polytheists arranged a meeting, they would have failed to keep its time; God instead brought them together without an appointment.
rows.anchor: ولو تواعدتم } أنتم والمشركون، { لاختلفتم في الميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought about an inevitable matter, exalting Islam and its adherents while humiliating idolatry and its adherents.
rows.anchor: ليعز الإسلام وأهله، ويذل الشرك وأهله

words: لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَىَّ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome lets one perish in disbelief or live by faith, each on the basis of clear proof.
rows.anchor: ليهلك من هلك عن بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust towns were idolatrous; God's taking means His seizure, painful means hurting, and severe means intense.
rows.anchor: أي مشركة، { إن أخذه } ، يعني بطشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of towns is a lesson for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني إن في هلاك القرى لعبرة

words: ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌۭ مَّجْمُوعٌۭ لَّهُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌۭ مَّشْهُودٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord and angels witness the gathering of creatures for presentation and reckoning.
rows.anchor: شهد الرب والملائكة لعرض الخلائق وحسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Resurrection is delayed only until its appointed time.
rows.anchor: يعني وما نؤخر يوم القيامة إلا لأجل موقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When that Day comes, no soul speaks except by God's permission; people are divided into wretched and happy.
rows.anchor: لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } بإذن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafir is like a donkey's final bray and shaheeq like its first; Abu al-Abbas Thaʿlab says zafir comes from the whole body and shaheeq from the chest.
rows.anchor: زفير } ، يعني آخر نهيق الحمار

rows.speaker: أبو العباس ثعلب
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas Thaʿlab distinguishes them by saying zafir comes from the whole body and shaheeq from the chest.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العباس ثعلب: الزفير من البدن كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched do not die in Hell; as the heavens and earth endure for worldly people, they remain there and do not leave.
rows.anchor: كما تدوم السموات والأرض لأهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is for monotheists, whom God brings out of the Fire so they do not abide there forever.
rows.anchor: فاستثنى الموحدين الذين يخرجون من النار لا يخلدون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra interprets the exception as allowing for God's addition of further creatures to the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني سوى ما شاء ربك من زيادة الخلق في النار

words: فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the heavens and earth endure for worldly people, the happy remain in Paradise and do not leave it.
rows.anchor: ثم لا يخرجون منها، وكذلك السعداء في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the exception means monotheists whom God brings out of the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني الموحدين الذين يخرجون من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift is never cut off from them.
rows.anchor: يعني غير مقطوع عنهم أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether each female carries a male or female, as in 31:34, and whether the fetus is sound or otherwise.
rows.anchor: من ذكر وأنثى، كقوله في لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What wombs diminish refers to a reduction from the nine months of pregnancy, like water receding.
rows.anchor: وما تنقص الأرحام من الأشهر التسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What wombs increase includes a fully developed child and additional growth in its mother's womb.
rows.anchor: من تمام الولد والزيادة في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows when the child will emerge from the womb and how long it will remain there.
rows.anchor: قدر خروج الولد من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen includes the fetus in the womb and everything unseen; the witnessed includes the fetus and all else visible.
rows.anchor: يعني غيب الولد في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the greatest, with none greater than Him, and is exalted above His creation.
rows.anchor: الرفيع فوق خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Book to Muhammad to bring people from darkness into light, meaning from idolatry to faith, by their Lord's command.
rows.anchor: لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is the religion; the Mighty is mighty in His dominion and the Praiseworthy is praised by His creatures for His command.
rows.anchor: يعني إلى دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is Mecca, which was a place of safety for its people in the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: يعني مكة، فكان أمنا لهم في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bani means Ibrahim's children; he knew his descendants would differ in their affirmation of God's oneness.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن ذريته مختلفون في التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols led many people astray through worshipping them.
rows.anchor: يعني أضللن بعبادتهن كثيرا من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows Ibrahim follows his religion and belongs to his community.
rows.anchor: على ديني، { فإنه مني } على ملتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who disobeys Ibrahim is a disbeliever; God may forgive, lead the person to repent, and guide them to monotheism, as in 33:24.
rows.anchor: أن تتوب عليه، فتهديه إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants were Ishmael in particular; the barren, waterless valley was Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني إسماعيل ابني خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the House sacred against unlawful acts; Muqatil notes fronting in the clause, whose purpose is that they pray and worship there.
rows.anchor: حرمه لئلا يستحل فيه ما لا يحل

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks that some people yearn toward Ishmael and his descendants and that they receive fruits; specifying some avoids crowding by Haraz and Daylam.
rows.anchor: ولو قال: اجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Ibrahim hid was his distress about Ishmael being in a foreign land without livelihood or water.
rows.anchor: من أمر إسماعيل في نفسي من الجزع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Ibrahim made known was his statement that he settled descendants in a barren valley, meaning Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني مكة، فهذي الذي أعلن

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After migrating to the Holy Land, Ibrahim received Ishmael by Hajar at age sixty and Isaac at seventy; all prophets descend from Isaac except Muhammad, from Ishmael.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم يومئذ ابن ستين سنة، ووهب له إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks that his descendants also establish prayer.
rows.anchor: فاجعلهم أيضا مقيمين الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks God to answer his prayer that he and his descendants establish prayer.
rows.anchor: واستجب دعائي في إقامة الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents means Ibrahim's two parents; he also asks forgiveness for believers on the Day the reckoning begins.
rows.anchor: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي } ، يعني أبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people Muhammad is commanded to warn are Meccan unbelievers; the wrongdoers are Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة، { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Hereafter, the polytheists ask to return to worldly life and be delayed briefly, promising to answer the call to monotheism and follow Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فيسألون الرجعة إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls their former oath that no dead person would be raised, as stated in 16:38.
rows.anchor: لا يبعث الله من يموت

words: وَسَكَنتُمْ فِى مَسَٰكِنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations, including the people of Hud, wronged themselves and were punished in this world; their fate and examples warned Meccan unbelievers to worship God alone.
rows.anchor: يعني قوم هود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod ibn Canaan, who argued with Ibrahim and first ruled the whole earth, built a tower in Babylon to reach heaven; its roof collapsed. Muqatil identifies the plot with a coffin and four vultures.
rows.anchor: بنى صرحا ببابل زعم ليتناول إله السماء

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that Nimrod made a coffin with upper and lower doors, tied four vultures to it with red meat as bait, and rose skyward with two men inside; one saw earth below like a white ring.
rows.anchor: نحت التابوت، وجعل له بابا من أعلاه، وبابا من أسفله

words: وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil compares the phrase to 17:73, which he glosses as their having nearly succeeded.
rows.anchor: يعني وقد كادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town is destroyed at a time fixed in the Preserved Tablet; Mecca's punishment was likewise appointed, namely killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: موقوت في اللوح المحفوظ إلى أجل

words: مَا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No punished nation can advance or delay its appointed term.
rows.anchor: ما يتقدمون من أجلهم، ولا يتأخرون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says the insult was revealed concerning Quraysh men Abdullah ibn Umayya ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who called the Prophet mad; dhikr means Quran.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أمية بن المغيرة المخزومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand angels as proof Muhammad is a sent prophet; had angels descended, they would have brought punishment.
rows.anchor: ولو نزلت الملائكة لنزلت إليهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels came down with punishment, the Meccan unbelievers would not be given respite before being punished.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يناظروا حتى يعذبوا، يعني كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Quran revealed to Muhammad; God protects it because satans cannot reach it, rebutting the claim that a satan teaches the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن الشياطين لا يصلون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fashioned Adam's creation, breathed into him, and commanded the angels to prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: يعني سويت خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the angels in the earth prostrated.
rows.anchor: الذين هم في الأرض

words: إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was excepted from the angels and refused to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: لآدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those worshipped besides God by Meccan unbelievers are al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat, and Hubal.
rows.anchor: يعني اللات، والعزى، ومناة، وهبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols create nothing, not even a fly, and are themselves carved by their worshippers' hands.
rows.anchor: ذبابا ولا غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are dead and lifeless: they cannot speak, hear, see, benefit, or harm, and have no spirit.
rows.anchor: ولا تنفع، ولا تضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan unbelievers do not know when they will be resurrected and are guessers, as in 27:65.
rows.anchor: نظيرها في سورة النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one and alone to be worshipped; those rejecting the Hereafter deny resurrection and recompense, reject God's oneness, and are arrogant.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يصدقون بالبعث الذي فيه جزاء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths mean covenants; using them as a stratagem means deceit, and breaking a covenant makes one slip in religion and taste punishment for blocking people from Islam.
rows.anchor: يعني العهد

words: وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not trade fidelity to God's covenant for small worldly gain; God's reward for fulfilling it is better than immediate gain.
rows.anchor: ولا تبيعوا الوفاء بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth people possess perishes, while the reward with God in the Hereafter is lasting; those who persevere in fulfilling covenants receive the best reward and have sins overlooked.
rows.anchor: من الأموال { ينفد } ، يعني يفنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Imru al-Qays ibn Abbas al-Kindi when Abdan ibn Ashra al-Hadrami judged his claim to land and a house.
rows.anchor: حين حكم عبدان بن أشرع الحضرمي في أرضه

words: مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer affirms God's oneness; believing men and women who act righteously receive a good life in this world and the best reward in the Hereafter, with sins left unrecompensed.
rows.anchor: يعني مصدق بتوحيد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta-Ha means O man in Syriac.
rows.anchor: يعني يا رجل وهو بالسريانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi said the Prophet suffered for leaving his fathers' religion and called him wretched after he said he was sent as a mercy; the verse answered them.
rows.anchor: إنك لتشقى حين تركت دين آبائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was sent as a reminder for whoever fears God, from the Creator of the earth and seven high heavens, not to make Muhammad suffer.
rows.anchor: ممن خلق الأرض } كلها { والسماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object in Moses' right hand was his staff; God asked while intending to transform it into a serpent.
rows.anchor: يعنى عصاه كانت بيده اليمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses leaned on the staff for support while walking.
rows.anchor: يقول: أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He struck trees so leaves fell for his young flock to eat.
rows.anchor: أخبط بها الشجر فيتهاش الورق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other uses included carrying provisions and a waterskin, producing food and water, shining at night, turning the flock back, protecting it, and killing snakes and scorpions by God's permission.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى، عليه السلام، يحمل زاده وسقاءه على عصاه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that Gabriel gave Moses the staff at night as he headed to Midian; its name was Nafa.
rows.anchor: واسم العصا نفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded Moses to throw the staff.
rows.anchor: { قال } الله عز وجل: { ألقها يموسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff became a moving male serpent on its belly, hairy and crested; Moses feared taking hold of it.
rows.anchor: ذكرا أشعر، له عرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses not to fear; when Moses grasped the serpent's tail, it returned to its original form as a staff.
rows.anchor: فصارت عصا كما كانت

words: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' palm came from his garment white without leprosy, shining like the sun and dazzling sight.
rows.anchor: فخرجت بيضاء لها شعاع كشعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand was another sign besides the staff.
rows.anchor: آية أخرى سوى العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the hand as the greater, more wondrous sign and links it to 79:20.
rows.anchor: فأراه الآية الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned away from the truth and assembled his sorcerers as his scheme.
rows.anchor: أعرض فرعون عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warned them not to falsely claim that the hand and staff were not from God but were magic.
rows.anchor: لقولهم: إن اليد والعصا ليستا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yashtikum means God will destroy them all with punishment; whoever invents a lie about God has lost.
rows.anchor: فيسحتكم } يعني فهلككم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians disputed among themselves, as in 18:21; they whispered secretly away from Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: نظيرها في الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They said Moses and Aaron aimed to expel people from Egypt and take their leading men; amthal means distinguished men of intelligence and honor whom people would follow instead of Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: من أهل العقول والشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells his magicians to assemble their magic and come together; whoever prevails will succeed.
rows.anchor: يعني سحركم

words: إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians ask Moses whether he will throw his staff first or let them throw first.
rows.anchor: { وإما أن نكون } نحن

words: يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ropes and staffs appeared to Moses to move by magic, although the ropes did not move.
rows.anchor: وكانت حبالا وهي لا تتحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared people would doubt him and not follow if the magicians seemed to match his sign, including his existing followers.
rows.anchor: أن يشكوا فيه فلا يتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel conveyed God's reassurance that Moses would be victor; Muqatil compares it with 3:139 and 47:35, where being uppermost means victorious.
rows.anchor: هذا قول جبريل لموسى، عليه السلام، عن أمر ربه، عز وجل، وهو على يمينه

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians refuse to choose Pharaoh over the signs, meaning the hand and staff, or their Creator; they tell him to judge them by cutting and crucifixion, since he rules only this life.
rows.anchor: يعنون اليد والعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith means affirming God's oneness.
rows.anchor: يقول: إنا صدقنا بتوحيد الله

words: خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their errors were their magic, including what Pharaoh forced them to perform; God is better and more enduring than Pharaoh, who dies while God alone remains, answering Pharaoh's claim in 20:71.
rows.anchor: يعنى ما جبرتناعليه { من السحر والله خير وأبقى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A criminal here is a polytheist in the Hereafter; Muqatil addresses Pharaoh as such.
rows.anchor: وأنت هو يا فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live in a way that benefits them; Muqatil cites 87:1 as a parallel.
rows.anchor: فتنفعه الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer affirms God's oneness; righteous actions earn the elevated ranks and virtues of Paradise.
rows.anchor: الفضائل الرفيعة في الجنة

words: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivers flow beneath the gardens, whose inhabitants never die; enduring there is the reward of those who purify themselves.
rows.anchor: { جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار } يعني تحت البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's exaltation means that He is above; He is true King because everything else and other gods are false.
rows.anchor: وما سواه من الآلهة باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel had not finished the revelation before the Prophet began repeating its opening; God tells him to wait until Gabriel completes it.
rows.anchor: لم يفرغ جبريل، عليه السلام، من آخر الكلام، حتى يتكلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بأوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says the request to increase in knowledge means to increase in Quran.
rows.anchor: يعني قرآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muhammad, God charged Adam not to eat from the tree.
rows.anchor: ألا يأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiya means Adam abandoned the charge, as do the same verb forms in 20:88, 32:14, and 5:14.
rows.anchor: يقول: فترك آدم العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam had no endurance to refrain from eating from the tree.
rows.anchor: يعني صبرا عن أكلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the spirit was breathed into Adam, the angels prostrated at God's command, but Iblis refused.
rows.anchor: ثم استثنى فقال: { إلا إبليس } لم يسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warned Adam and Eve that Satan would make Adam toil: before sin he ate freely without working, but afterward worked for his food.
rows.anchor: كان يأكل من الجنة رغدا من غير أن يعمل بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Garden Adam would neither hunger nor go unclothed.
rows.anchor: ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى
